absent: Numeric values and bit positions of mount, superblock, lookup and configuration constants.
Full definitions of filesystem context, superblock, mount, path, dentry and filename structures beyond observed fields.
Behaviour of tree acquisition, security gates, dentry cache shrink, pin killing and filesystem specific reconfigure callbacks.
Locking rules for namespace semaphore, mount hash and superblock exclusion beyond observed acquire release sites.
Error codes and user visible effects for failure paths not shown in fragments.
Implementation of graft, attach, expiry, notification and chroot reference updates during pivot and loopback.

findings.text: System entry for picking an existing mount for reconfiguration requires mount privilege and accepts only documented option bits for close on exec, symlink nofollow, automount suppression and empty path acceptance. It resolves a target path with follow and automount behaviour adjusted by those options, rejects targets that are not a mount root, and on success returns a descriptor for a fresh configuration context in reconfiguration parameter state with allocated logging.

Configuration entry validates its descriptor and command class before touching user memory. Flag, string, binary, path and file descriptor parameter forms each have distinct validity rules for key, value and auxiliary argument presence and size. After copying user inputs with bounded lengths, it serializes against other callers through the context user API mutex and delegates to a locked dispatcher, then releases any user obtained string, blob, path name or file reference not stolen by lower layers.
Early boot helper for pivot root resolves two directory paths in kernel space with follow semantics and delegates to a path based pivot operation, propagating lookup failures.
Early boot helper for mount resolves a directory path in kernel space with follow semantics, invokes a path based mount operation with supplied device, type, flags and data, then releases the path.

Capability probe for filesystem context creation reports administrator privilege in initial namespace for ordinary types and administrator privilege in the context user namespace for user namespace mountable types.

Reconfiguration path moves a context from parameter gathering to reconfiguring state, checks administrator privilege in superblock user namespace, holds superblock writers exclusion across the superblock reconfiguration, marks failure on error and cleans the context on success.

Creation command is only accepted in create parameter state. It checks mount capability, records exclusivity, transitions to creating, obtains the tree, performs a security gate for kernel mount, releases superblock writers exclusion on success and ends in awaiting mount state, or in failed state on error.

Locked configuration dispatcher first finishes any pending clean context work, routes create, exclusive create and reconfigure commands to their dedicated handlers, and routes all other parameter commands to a parameter parser only when the context remains in a parameter gathering state for create or reconfigure, otherwise reporting busy.

Superblock writers exclusion is held for write across tree acquisition and reconfiguration. Creation path expects the exclusion to be already held after tree acquisition and releases it before reporting awaiting mount. Reconfiguration path acquires and releases it around the superblock update.

User API mutex serializes configuration calls on one context. Propagation type change serializes with exclusive namespace guard plus a read guard for mount state and touches the namespace after updates. Pivot and loopback paths use a mount lock macro around target resolution and a global mount hash lock around tree surgery.

User path copying first attempts an embedded small name buffer and falls back to a larger dynamically allocated buffer when the name reaches the embedded limit, enforcing empty path policy, overlong rejection and audit capture, with distinct handling for kernel supplied names.

Path based mount sanitizes historic magic, terminates option data, rejects unprivileged and unknown flag combinations, applies a security gate and privilege check, derives per mount point and per superblock flag sets with relatime default and remount atime preservation, then dispatches to reconfigure, remount, bind, propagation change, move or new mount handlers based on request bits.

Pivot root requires privilege, passes a security gate, resolves current root, validates that new and old locations are mounted mount points with parents below root, rejects shared propagation participants, locked mounts, unlinked targets and loops, then under hash lock swaps the root and old mounts, transfers lock state, refreshes namespace time, detaches expiry and notifies watchers before switching process root references.

Remount to read only preparation uses a racy fast check on removal count, then under mount read guard iteratively holds writers on each writable mount of the superblock, rechecks removal count, starts a read only state change on success and always clears hold markers before returning.

Superblock reconfiguration validates flag mask and frozen state, runs a security gate, derives read only versus read write transition intent from mask and current state, kills group pins when needed for read only transition with revalidation, shrinks dentry cache, blocks new writers for transitions, invokes filesystem specific reconfigure when present with distinct forced versus strict error handling, commits flag subset and invalidates block device on read only transition.

Propagation change requires a mounted target, maps request bits to exactly one of shared, private, slave or unbindable with recursion preserved, checks namespace attachment and administrator privilege, preallocates group identifiers for shared case, then walks the affected mounts applying the new propagation and refreshing namespace time.

Loopback bind resolves a source path with follow and automount, rejects empty names and namespace file loops based on namespace identifier ordering, validates the destination mount lock, duplicates the tree with namespace file copying semantics, rejects recursive copies that carry unexpected namespace files, and grafts the copy or tears it down under hash lock on failure.

Observed configuration context carries a phase indicator, exclusivity marker, root dentry reference, filesystem type, user namespace, operation vector, security blob, superblock flag set and mask, and a user API mutex plus logging state. Phase values distinguish create parameters, creating, awaiting mount, reconfigure parameters, reconfiguring and failed.

Observed superblock carries writer freeze state, removal count, pin list, mount list, root, user namespace, block device, type and flag set plus a read only remount marker manipulated with barriers. Observed mount carries per mount flags, propagation linkage including share list, slave list, master pointer, group identifier and unbindable marker, plus expiry linkage and a pointer field whose low bit encodes a writer hold.

Observed parameter record carries a key plus a discriminated value that can be flag, string with length, binary blob with length, file name with directory descriptor and length, or open file with directory descriptor. String keys and values use bounded user duplication, binary blobs use bounded duplication with explicit size, paths use name lookup objects, files use raw file references.

Writer hold is a low bit stolen in a mount linkage pointer with set, test and clear helpers. Holding writers stores the bit then issues a full barrier before summing per CPU writer counts, so counted writers cannot be missed. Read only state change markers use write barriers paired with read side checks to order flag visibility.

Reconfiguration fails busy when writers are frozen or removal activity is observed, fails access when a block device is read only but read write is requested, and may drop and reacquire superblock exclusion while killing pins, requiring revalidation of root and frozen state. Forced mode proceeds despite filesystem errors with a warning, while strict mode cancels the read only transition and returns the error.

Mount with mand lock flag triggers a one time deprecation warning and is otherwise ignored. Pivot and propagation paths reject shared mounts and related parents to avoid propagation surprises, and pivot additionally rejects locked mounts, unlinked dentries, non mount points, absolute roots and unreachable old locations.
Interface defines option FSPICK_CLOEXEC plus option FSPICK_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW plus option FSPICK_NO_AUTOMOUNT plus option FSPICK_EMPTY_PATH for the pick operation.

Interface defines commands FSCONFIG_SET_FLAG plus FSCONFIG_SET_STRING plus FSCONFIG_SET_BINARY plus FSCONFIG_SET_PATH plus FSCONFIG_SET_PATH_EMPTY plus FSCONFIG_SET_FD plus FSCONFIG_CMD_CREATE plus FSCONFIG_CMD_CREATE_EXCL plus FSCONFIG_CMD_RECONFIGURE for the configuration operation.

Mount interface distinguishes per mount point options MNT_READONLY plus MNT_NOSUID plus MNT_NODEV plus MNT_NOEXEC plus MNT_NOATIME plus MNT_NODIRATIME plus MNT_RELATIME plus MNT_NOSYMFOLLOW and request bits MS_REMOUNT plus MS_BIND plus MS_MOVE plus MS_SHARED plus MS_PRIVATE plus MS_SLAVE plus MS_UNBINDABLE plus MS_REC plus related atime and read only bits.

Lookup behaviour uses distinct bits LOOKUP_FOLLOW plus LOOKUP_AUTOMOUNT plus LOOKUP_EMPTY plus LOOKUP_DIRECTORY. Configuration phases include FS_CONTEXT_CREATE_PARAMS plus FS_CONTEXT_CREATING plus FS_CONTEXT_AWAITING_MOUNT plus FS_CONTEXT_RECONF_PARAMS plus FS_CONTEXT_RECONFIGURING plus FS_CONTEXT_FAILED. Superblock flag handling uses SB_RDONLY plus SB_FORCE plus related synchronous and attribute bits.

Change propagation helper converts a mount among shared, slave, private and unbindable forms, managing share list membership, group identifier lifetime, slave linkage and master pointer with transfer of propagation when leaving shared state.
Mounted test reports true when a path mount root equals its dentry.
Path based mount dispatcher and pivot root operation are exported for early boot and general mount handling.
